title: High-Dimensional Molecular Feature Selection for Acute Oral Toxicity Prediction

slides.title: High-Dimensional Molecular Feature Selection
body: Combining Sure Independence Screening with Elastic Net Regularization Machine Learning in Computational Toxicology

slides.title: Context: The Problem
body: In drug discovery, testing each candidate compound for toxicity is expensive and slow:
Testing timeline: weeks to months per compound
Bottleneck: hundreds of synthetic candidates need screening
Can we predict toxicity from molecular structure alone—before expensive physical testing?
How do we identify the critical few?

slides.title: The Dataset: QSAR Oral Toxicity
body: Class Imbalance: 9% toxic, 91% non-toxic compounds. Standard accuracy is useless—a model predicting "always non-toxic" is 91% accurate but worthless.
Solution: Use PR-AUC, F1-Score, and MCC instead. Apply balanced class weights during training.

slides.title: Our Approach: Four Stages
body: Remove zero-variance features. Stratified 70-15-15 train-val-test split.
Rank 1,024 features by chi-squared statistics. Select top 40.
Measure PR-AUC, F1, MCC, ROC-AUC. Ablation study: SIS impact. Feature importance analysis.

slides.title: Sure Independence Screening (SIS)
body: A statistical method that ranks features by their marginal association with the target.
For each molecular feature, we build a 2×2 contingency table:
Interpretation: High χ² = strong feature-toxicity association.
Fast: O(p) where p = feature count
Result: Top 40 features capture most signal

slides.title: Seven Models: Baseline to Proposed
body: Random Forest: 100 trees, depth=15. Strong nonlinear baseline.

slides.title: Proposed: SIS + Elastic Net
body: First: SIS reduces to 40 features. Then: Elastic Net learns sparse coefficients. Combines statistical screening with modern regularization.
LASSO (L1): Encourages zerosRidge (L2): Smooth shrinkageElastic Net (L1+L2): Hybrid

slides.title: Why These Metrics Matter
body: With 91% non-toxic baseline, accuracy is misleading. Predicting "always non-toxic" = 91% accurate but useless.
PR-AUC: Precision-Recall curve. Best for imbalanced data. Focuses on minority class (toxic) detection.
F1-Score: Harmonic mean of precision & recall. Single number summary of balance.
MCC: Matthews Correlation Coefficient. Robust correlation measure. Ranges -1 to +1.
ROC-AUC: True positive vs false positive tradeoff at all thresholds.

slides.title: Results: Model Comparison on Test Set
body: SIS + Elastic Net achieves best PR-AUC (0.340, most important for imbalance).
Random Forest wins on F1 (0.806) but uses all 1,024 features (black box).
The tradeoff: Accept slightly lower accuracy for 40 interpretable features.

slides.title: Ablation Study: Does SIS Actually Help?
body: Is SIS actually improving performance, or just luck?
Train Elastic Net with 5 different L1-L2 mixing parameters (α: 0 to 1) in two conditions:
by +3–5% F1-score across all α values. This proves: SIS filtering is essential in high dimensions.
Why? With 1,024 features and ~700 training samples, noise features dominate. SIS pre-filters to top 40 signals, giving regularizer a fighting chance.

slides.title: Top 5 Toxicophore Fragments
body: A ranked list of 40 molecular fragments that predict toxicity. Chemists can use immediately:
Chemist synthesizes a candidate drug. Instant screen: contains Feature 878? 777? 155? If 3+ critical fragments present → predicted toxic → avoid this structure.
Actionable screening checklistfor drug discovery teams
Impact: Saves months of testing. Prevents synthesis of obviously toxic compounds.

slides.title: Key Findings & Conclusions
body: SIS is effective. 96% dimensionality reduction while improving F1 by 3–5%. High-dimensional noise is real.
Interpretability wins. SIS + Elastic Net trades ~5% accuracy for 1,000× simpler model. Worth it.
Imbalance matters. Wrong metrics (accuracy) fail. Right metrics (PR-AUC, F1, MCC) reveal truth.
Chemists understand 40 molecular fragments. Can't explain 1,024 features.
Works for any toxicity endpoint (liver, kidney, cardiac). Transfer learning possible.
In drug discovery, converting 1,024 opaque features into 40 actionable molecular alerts is the real innovation—not squeezing out 5% more accuracy.
